claims.scope_statement: Per-dataset evidence is monitored, not 'verified'. The catalogue reports observed probe outcomes from the published MCP server; downstream consumers must re-run verify_dataset() to obtain a fresh receipt.
claims.re_audit_trigger: Any change to scripts/gen_per_dataset_receipt.py or any new per-dataset claim in copy.
claims.notes: The phrase 'verified datasets' implies uniform coverage that does not exist. Replace with 'monitored datasets' or 'datasets with published receipts'.

claims.scope_statement: DataPulse is authoritative for the registry itself (the catalogue and machine advertisements). It is NOT authoritative for upstream sources — those upstream maintainers own their own authoritative signals.
claims.re_audit_trigger: Any change to docs/agent-quickstart.md or new docs/ pages referencing authority.

allowed_occurrences.justification: The phrase 'authoritative' is qualified in this occurrence to refer to the DataPulse registry, not underlying sources. The sentence structure makes this scope explicit.
This is a 'Never upgrade X to Y' guideline for future contributors — it names the phrase precisely so future copy does not regress to it. The lint should not flag this occurrence.

claims.notes: All future occurrences outside the two annotated sites must be qualified by 'registry' or 'catalogue' within 5 words of 'authoritative'.

claims.scope_statement: Per the 2026-08-17 retraction discipline, DataPulse MY does not make 'first' or 'pioneer' claims about the agency-verification category.
claims.evidence_source: notes/2026-08-17-retraction-discipline.md (if it exists; otherwise the September-1 quiet-excellence memo)
claims.re_audit_trigger: Any new retraction-discipline revision or any new headline claim.
claims.notes: Note: 'first' as in 'first issue', 'first having to', or 'first request' is allowed — this rule targets promotional novelty phrases like 'first to provide', 'pioneer of', 'industry first'.

claims.scope_statement: Coverage is partial. The per-dataset receipt generator is per-call, not per-dataset-persisted for every dataset; portability covers some, not all 389.
claims.re_audit_trigger: If a refresh produces stable receipts for all datasets, this claim can be retired; until then it stays forbidden.
claims.notes: The phrase 'per-dataset receipt' (without 'every/all') is allowed in llms.txt and tool descriptions because it describes the verification method.

claims.phrase_pattern: \b(freshness verified|freshness is verified|freshness has been verified)\b
claims.scope_statement: Freshness is observed per-probe. The 10-status taxonomy exposes `stale`, `aging`, `unknown-freshness`, etc. — never a uniform 'verified' claim.
claims.notes: Replace with 'freshness is reported' or 'freshness is observed' if needed.

claims.scope_statement: Tool count is 18 at HEAD. Any numeric claim about MCP tool count must be a generated artifact (e.g. from mcp.json or the per-tool cards listing), not hard-coded.
claims.re_audit_trigger: Any new tool addition or removal — count delta must be regenerated.
claims.notes: Pattern matches literal numbers like '16 tools', '17 tools', '18 tools', etc. The rule: any numeric MCP tool count claim must come from the auto-regenerated resource, not be hand-typed.

claims.scope_statement: Quiet-excellence memo language. Do not promote any 'uncrowded' framing; let external observers draw that conclusion from the evidence.
claims.re_audit_trigger: If the quiet-excellence memo is retired or revised.

claims.scope_statement: Mathematical use of 'standard' is allowed only in files where it is the term of art (statistical methodology).
claims.re_audit_trigger: Any new statistical file or new health-methodology revision.

allowed_occurrences.justification: Term of art for the probe's statistical outlier test.

claims.scope_statement: Any verifier in scripts/verify_*.py that depends on health/history.jsonl must check for the file's existence as its first step. If the file is missing or zero-sized, the verifier exits with an INFO message (and the appropriate exit code per test expectations) instead of crashing with FileNotFoundError. Source-card verifier (scripts/verify_source_cards.py), failure-corpus verifier (scripts/verify_failure_corpus.py), and any future live-history-anchored verifier must follow the same pattern.
claims.re_audit_trigger: Any new health-history-anchored verifier must be checked for the same missing-history handling.

allowed_occurrences.line_range_or_pattern: argparse.parse_args() default + main() first step before any history_path.open()
allowed_occurrences.justification: Documented invariant. Verifier checks for history_path.exists() and exits cleanly with INFO when missing.

allowed_occurrences.line_range_or_pattern: main() first step before any history_path.open()

claims.notes: Retroactive audit-record from HS-05. The pattern was implemented in commits b13f885a3 and 79402d651 (DP-08 chain) after PR CI failed on missing history in CI.

claims.scope_statement: scripts/verify_local_public_parity.py MUST NOT include a deterministic_regen dimension that byte-compares docs/index.html against an in-memory render of itself. Such a comparison is too strict for files whose content drifts by probe-cycle (e.g., embed_dashboard_data.py output that absorbs the latest health/latest.json). Regen parity is the responsibility of scripts/verify_release_reproducible.py, which controls regen timing. The parity verifier is restricted to live/local read-back across 7 dimensions: dataset_count, taxonomy, source_commit, manifest_schema, attestation_subject, receipts, public_routes.
claims.evidence_source: scripts/verify_local_public_parity.py (current shape after commit bbb95ea7d) + scripts/verify_release_reproducible.py (canonical owner of regen parity)
claims.re_audit_trigger: If regen parity must be re-introduced into parity verifier, add it as a soft tolerance check (size band, schema-shape parity) NOT as a byte-exact equality.

allowed_occurrences.line_range_or_pattern: verify() returns 7 dimensions and skips deterministic_regen
allowed_occurrences.justification: Documented scope. Regen parity is owned by verify_release_reproducible.py.

claims.notes: Retroactive audit-record from HS-05. The deterministic_regen dimension was removed in commit bbb95ea7d after PR CI failed with deterministic_regen size drift on a probe-driven file.
